Please is a free English verb borrowed through French from Latin placere; -please should not be presented as a suffix. English mob is a clipping of English mobile / mobility in the crowd sense, from Latin mobile vulgus fickle common people; ultimately mobilis from movere. It is an English lexical clipping, not a free Latin root meaning move. Its sole candidate source gloss is crowd. The current English base mob is an independent crowd noun produced by clipping; historical ancestry through mobilis does not itself prove mob- is the Latin movement stem.

English dentist was borrowed from French dentiste, formed from French dent tooth plus -iste; its i begins the agent suffix. The spelling denti spans the base and suffix, though the word belongs to the dent family.
Etymonline derives dentistry from dentist plus -ry, and dentist from French dentiste, dent plus -iste. Consequently the i in denti is inherited from the agent suffix, not a tooth combining form.
